description: ECDAT Versioned Knowledge Base of Post-Quantum, Hybrid, and Classical Cryptographic Algorithms

authorities_tracked.nist: National Institute of Standards and Technology (FIPS 203, FIPS 204, FIPS 205, SP 800-208)
authorities_tracked.anssi: Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (French Cybersecurity Agency PQC Scientific Opinions & Hybrid Transition Guidelines)
authorities_tracked.bsi: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (German Federal Office for Information Security Technical Guidelines BSI TR-02102)
authorities_tracked.nsa_cnsa: National Security Agency Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (CNSA 2.0 Transition Timelines)
authorities_tracked.ietf: Internet Engineering Task Force Post-Quantum Use in Protocols (PQUIP) and TLS Working Groups

characteristics.performance_profile: Extremely fast keygen and decapsulation; minimal CPU overhead.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Public key (800B) and ciphertext (768B) fit cleanly within standard 1500-byte Ethernet MTU.
migration_considerations.state_management: Stateless KEM. No state tracking or non-volatile storage required.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Faster than classical RSA-2048 and comparable to ECDH P-256.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Recommended for constrained embedded devices or low-bandwidth networks.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Supported in liboqs, OpenSSL 3.5, and standard PQC libraries.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Not recommended as sole mechanism by ANSSI/BSI; pair with classical ECDH in hybrid mode.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 1 (AES-128 equivalent). Approved for general use under FIPS 203.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Stage 2 hybrid mode required; standalone PQC not permitted for sensitive government systems.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Acceptable for Category 1 security; hybrid deployment strongly advised.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: NOT approved for CNSA 2.0. NSA mandates Category 5 (ML-KEM-1024) exclusively.

characteristics.performance_profile: Optimal security/performance balance. Sub-millisecond encapsulation and decapsulation.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Public key (1184B) approaches typical single-packet MTU (1500B); when paired in hybrid TLS ClientHello, message fragmentation can occur on poorly configured middleboxes.
migration_considerations.state_management: Stateless KEM. No non-volatile synchronization required.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Negligible latency increase; CPU cycles comparable to X25519.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Primary default target for enterprise general-purpose data-in-transit protection.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Broadly deployed across Chrome, Firefox, Cloudflare, OpenSSL 3.4+, BoringSSL, AWS KMS.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Deploy via hybrid groups (X25519MLKEM768) to protect against unforeseen lattice cryptanalysis.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 3 (AES-192 equivalent). Primary recommended general-purpose KEM.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Stage 2 hybrid mode mandatory. Recommends pairing with X25519 or P-256.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Recommended for general commercial systems in hybrid configuration.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: NOT approved for National Security Systems (NSS). CNSA 2.0 requires Level 5.
authority_recommendations.ietf: Core post-quantum KEM selected for TLS 1.3 hybrid key exchange.

characteristics.performance_profile: High security margin; slightly higher memory footprint and key sizes.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Public key (1568B) strictly exceeds standard 1500-byte Ethernet MTU, guaranteeing IP fragmentation or TLS record segmentation.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Well within hardware budget for enterprise servers; slightly higher bandwidth.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Mandatory for high-assurance, defense, and top-secret intelligence requirements.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Supported in OpenSSL 3.4+, liboqs, AWS KMS, and CNSA 2.0 compliant appliances.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Pair with P-384 or X448 for CNSA 2.0 dual-layer defense.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 5 (AES-256 equivalent). Highest security classification.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Approved for high-assurance environments in hybrid mode.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: MANDATORY for US National Security Systems under CNSA 2.0 (deployment timeline 2025-2030).

characteristics.performance_profile: Very fast verification; signature creation is faster than classical RSA.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Signature size (2.4 KB) significantly larger than classical ECDSA (64 B) or RSA (256 B); increases TLS certificate chain and handshake size.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Fast CPU verification; main bottleneck is network bandwidth and packet size expansion.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Recommended for embedded and client authentication certificates.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Standard implementations in OpenSSL 3.5, Bouncy Castle, WolfSSL.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Use composite signatures (draft-ietf-lamps-pq-composite-sigs) during transition.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 2 (SHA-256 equivalent). Approved under FIPS 204.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Suitable for general digital signature usage.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: NOT approved for CNSA 2.0. NSA mandates Category 5 (ML-DSA-87).
authority_recommendations.ietf: Draft standards active in LAMPS and TLS working groups.

characteristics.performance_profile: Balanced primary signature scheme. Extremely fast verification.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Public key (1.95 KB) + signature (3.3 KB) adds ~5.3 KB per certificate in PKI hierarchy.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Verification is ~10x faster than RSA-2048 verification.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Primary recommended post-quantum signature algorithm for enterprise PKI and code signing.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Growing adoption in PKI software, HashiCorp Vault, CFSSL.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Pair with ECDSA P-256 / P-384 in composite certificates for backward compatibility.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 3. Primary general-purpose signature scheme.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: NOT approved for NSS; NSA requires ML-DSA-87 for CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Highest security lattice signature. Fast verification, larger payload.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Signature (4.6 KB) requires buffer resizing in hardware security appliances.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Requires accommodating ~7.2 KB total public-key + signature footprint.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Mandatory for CNSA 2.0 classified and defense systems.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Supported in government-certified cryptographic modules and OpenSSL 3.5.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Pair with ECDSA P-384 or RSA-4096 in composite certificates.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 5. Highest security signature standard under FIPS 204.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: MANDATORY for US National Security Systems digital signatures under CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Compact public keys (32B); large signatures (7.8KB); slower signing speed.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Signatures exceed 7.8 KB; unsuited for high-throughput interactive TLS sessions.
migration_considerations.state_management: Stateless hash-based signature scheme. No non-volatile state synchronization risk.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Signing takes tens of milliseconds; verification is relatively fast.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Vital hedge against potential mathematical breakthroughs in structured lattice problems.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Supported in OpenSSL 3.5, liboqs, Bouncy Castle.
interoperability_considerations.pki_x509_support: OID registered under NIST Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR).
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Ideal conservative backup algorithm for root certificate authorities and document signing.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 1. Standardized as stateless hash-based alternative to lattice schemes.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Strongly endorses hash-based foundations due to mature, well-understood security reductions.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Recommended as conservative fallback if lattice assumptions are questioned.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Secondary backup signature scheme under CNSA 2.0.
authority_recommendations.ietf: Tracked in IETF LAMPS for PKIX certificates.

characteristics.performance_profile: Ultra-conservative hash-based security; signature size is ~29.8 KB.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Extremely large signatures (29.8 KB); cannot be transmitted over single IP packets.
migration_considerations.state_management: Stateless. Completely safe from state reuse vulnerabilities.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Heavy signature generation overhead; best for root CA and archival signing.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Use where long-term mathematical assurance outweighs bandwidth constraints.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Implemented in specialized PQC and archive signing tools.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Not suitable for interactive TLS.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST Category 5. Highest security stateless hash-based signature standard.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Approved as conservative backup under CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Extremely fast verification in hardware/ASIC; compact public key; finite signing capacity.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Moderate signature size (~2.5 KB); easily handled in bootloader and firmware blocks.
migration_considerations.state_management: CRITICAL HAZARD: Stateful scheme. Re-using a one-time signature index completely destroys private key security. Requires atomic non-volatile hardware state tracking.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Ideal for boot ROM and hardware root-of-trust verification.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Strictly restricted to firmware, operating system updates, and bootloader code signing. FORBIDDEN for ephemeral TLS, multi-threaded signing, or general PKI.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Supported in hardware security modules (HSMs), UEFI secure boot, and CNSA 2.0 bootloader stacks.
interoperability_considerations.pki_x509_support: Supported under RFC 8708 for CMS/firmware packages.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: HSMs must enforce monotonic hardware counters to prevent VM snapshot rollback attacks.

authority_recommendations.nist: Approved in NIST SP 800-208 exclusively for firmware and software update signing under strict state management.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Approved exclusively for embedded and firmware signing under certified hardware control.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Permitted with strict HSM-enforced state isolation.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: MANDATORY for firmware and software code signing under CNSA 2.0 (transition begins 2025).

characteristics.performance_profile: Very fast verification; multi-tree structure allows millions of signatures.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Signatures (~2.8 KB) fit well in firmware packages and update containers.
migration_considerations.state_management: CRITICAL HAZARD: Stateful scheme. Must never roll back private key state. Key reuse completely breaks security.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Fast verification in hardware; suitable for secure boot and microcode updates.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Approved exclusively for software/firmware updates. Never use for general-purpose messaging or interactive TLS.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Standardized in RFC 8391; supported in specialized HSMs and bootloaders.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Requires HSM with physical monotonic counters to survive power loss or VM rollbacks.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST SP 800-208 approved for software/firmware signing under certified state control.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Allowed exclusively for firmware signing with certified state protection.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Permitted with strict HSM-enforced state isolation.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Approved alternative to LMS under CNSA 2.0 for software and firmware signing.

characteristics.performance_profile: Industry workhorse for TLS 1.3. Total key share is 1216B (32B X25519 + 1184B ML-KEM-768).

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: ClientHello size increases by ~1.2 KB. 99.9% of modern networks pass without fragmentation.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Imperceptible latency overhead in production (benchmarked < 1.5ms additional handshake time).
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Recommended default for all enterprise TLS 1.3 endpoints transitioning to post-quantum protection.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Standardized IANA codepoint 0x11ec. Native in OpenSSL 3.4+, Chrome 131+, Cloudflare, AWS.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: If peer does not support 0x11ec, falls back seamlessly to classical X25519 without security downgrade.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST SP 800-227 (Draft) endorses hybrid KEMs for defense-in-depth transition.
authority_recommendations.anssi: MANDATORY Stage 2 hybrid configuration for all French government and critical infrastructure.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Recommended hybrid approach to mitigate lattice cryptanalytic risk.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Permitted during transition; NSA ultimate target is pure Level 5.
authority_recommendations.ietf: Standardized in IETF TLS Working Group under draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design.

characteristics.performance_profile: FIPS-compliant hybrid group combining NIST P-256 with ML-KEM-768.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Total key share is 1249 bytes; comfortably fits within standard MTU.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Negligible latency impact.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Recommended for regulated enterprise environments (BFSI, healthcare) requiring FIPS 140 classical components.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Standardized IANA codepoint 0x11ed. Supported in OpenSSL 3.4+, Windows Schannel preview, Java 24.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Falls back to P-256 if client or server does not support ML-KEM.

authority_recommendations.nist: Meets FIPS 140-3 requirements when FIPS-validated P-256 module is utilized.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Approved hybrid group for government communications.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Permitted during transition phase.

characteristics.performance_profile: High-assurance hybrid group combining X25519 with Level 5 ML-KEM-1024.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Key share (1600B) exceeds 1500-byte MTU; requires TCP segmentation handling.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Slightly higher bandwidth overhead.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Recommended for high-value data transmission requiring Level 5 quantum resilience.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Standardized IANA codepoint 0x11ee.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Seamless fallback to X25519.

authority_recommendations.nist: Level 5 quantum security.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Compatible with Level 5 requirements.

characteristics.performance_profile: Full CNSA 2.0 and FIPS-aligned high-assurance hybrid group.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Key share (1665B) will segment over standard MTU.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Higher compute and network overhead; targeted at classified/defense backbones.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Recommended for government, aerospace, and defense environments adhering to CNSA 2.0.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Standardized IANA codepoint 0x11ef.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Falls back to P-384.

authority_recommendations.nist: Level 5 quantum security; FIPS 140 compliant classical P-384.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: STRONGLY ALIGNED with CNSA 2.0 dual-layer transition recommendations.

characteristics.performance_profile: NTRU Prime lattice hybrid; default in OpenSSH since version 9.0.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Comfortably fits within SSH protocol packet frames.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Negligible for interactive and automated SSH sessions.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Current default in OpenSSH. Transitioning to ML-KEM-768 under modern OpenSSH 9.8+.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Supported across all OpenSSH 9.0+ installations worldwide.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Falls back to curve25519-sha256 if remote server is older than OpenSSH 9.0.

authority_recommendations.nist: Streamlined NTRU Prime was not selected in final NIST round; NIST standard is ML-KEM.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Acknowledges OpenSSH practical deployment; recommends migrating to ML-KEM long-term.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Recognized as effective interim defense against HNDL for SSH.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Not approved under CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Standardized FIPS 203 ML-KEM hybrid for SSH.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Fully compatible with standard SSH packet buffers.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Fast execution on modern CPU architectures.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Recommended target for modern enterprise SSH server and client configurations.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Supported in OpenSSH 9.8+ and PuTTY 0.81+.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Falls back to sntrup761x25519 or curve25519.

authority_recommendations.nist: Incorporates official FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768 standard.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Permitted during transition.
authority_recommendations.ietf: Draft draft-kampanakis-curdle-ssh-pq-kex active in CURDLE WG.

characteristics.performance_profile: Legacy experimental codepoint used during initial Chrome/Cloudflare experiments.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Same as standardized ML-KEM-768.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Low.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: MIGRATE IMMEDIATELY: Uses pre-standard Round 3 Kyber with unassigned codepoint 0x6399.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Deprecated in modern browsers; superseded by IANA standardized 0x11ec.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Deprecated codepoint must be disabled in favor of 0x11ec.

authority_recommendations.nist: Superseded by official FIPS 203 standard.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Never approved.

characteristics.performance_profile: Extremely fast classical Montgomery curve key exchange.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Minimal (32 bytes).
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Extremely low.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Retain as classical anchor in hybrid schemes (X25519MLKEM768).

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Universally supported across TLS 1.3 implementations.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Standard fallback.

authority_recommendations.nist: NIST SP 800-131A approved classically; vulnerable to quantum computers.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Must be phased out under CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Standard classical Weierstrass curve key exchange.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Minimal (65 bytes uncompressed).
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Hardware accelerated on modern CPUs.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Pair with ML-KEM-768 in SecP256r1MLKEM768.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Universal worldwide support in TLS 1.2 and 1.3.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Standard.

authority_recommendations.nist: Classically compliant under FIPS 186-5; must migrate to PQC.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Must be replaced under CNSA 2.0 timeline.

characteristics.performance_profile: High-security classical curve (192-bit classical security level).

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Minimal (97 bytes).
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Moderate CPU cycles.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Pair with ML-KEM-1024 for high-security hybrid transitions.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Universal in enterprise and government systems.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Standard.

authority_recommendations.nist: Classically approved.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Previously CNSA 1.0; migrating to ML-KEM-1024 under CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Deprecated static key transport without forward secrecy.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Standard.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: High private key operation overhead.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: ELIMINATE: Lacks forward secrecy and completely broken by Shor's algorithm.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Removed in TLS 1.3.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Must be prohibited.

authority_recommendations.nist: Disallowed in modern TLS; lacks forward secrecy.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Strictly prohibited.

characteristics.performance_profile: Finite-field Diffie-Hellman ephemeral key exchange.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Standard.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Compute intensive compared to elliptic curves.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Migrate directly to hybrid ML-KEM.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Deprecated in modern deployments due to Logjam vulnerabilities.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Fallback to ECDHE or hybrid.

authority_recommendations.nist: Minimum 2048-bit required classically.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Disallowed under CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Very fast public key verification; slower private key signing.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Compact signatures (256-384B); well supported across all network gear.
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Baseline standard.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Completely broken by Shor's algorithm. Plan dual-signing / composite transition to ML-DSA.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Universal support worldwide.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Standard.

authority_recommendations.nist: 2048-bit minimum through 2030; must transition to ML-DSA/SLH-DSA.
authority_recommendations.anssi: Minimum 2048-bit through 2030; transition to hybrid signatures.
authority_recommendations.bsi: Minimum 2048-bit; BSI recommends migration planning now.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Must be completely phased out of NSS by 2030 under CNSA 2.0.

characteristics.performance_profile: Extremely compact signatures (64B); fast signing; moderate verification.

migration_considerations.mtu_impact: Smallest signature footprint (64 bytes).
migration_considerations.state_management: Stateless (requires secure nonces or deterministic RFC 6979).
migration_considerations.performance_overhead: Low.
migration_considerations.crypto_agility_guidance: Completely broken by Shor's algorithm. Plan transition to ML-DSA-65 or composite certificates.

interoperability_considerations.client_server_support: Universal support in modern systems.
interoperability_considerations.fallback_handling: Standard.

authority_recommendations.nist: Approved classically; vulnerable to quantum computers.
authority_recommendations.nsa_cnsa: Must be phased out by 2030 under CNSA 2.0.
